findings.title: dayjs objects compared with === always evaluates to false
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable, the condition `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two distinct dayjs object references with `===`, which is always false. This branch was meant to detect a blocked-day override (where start equals end, i.e. the host marked the whole day unavailable). Because the check never fires, the callback falls through and returns undefined; find() then yields nothing, but dateOverrideExist was already set to true, so `if (dateOverrideExist) return true` makes every slot on that day bookable — the exact opposite of the intended behavior. A fixed host who uses a date override to block a whole day on a round-robin event will still be shown as available. Use `.isSame()` to compare the two instants.

findings.title: Slot end computed from slotStartTime, breaking working-hours check
findings.body: In the new working-hours check inside checkIfIsAvailable, `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` is a copy-paste of the `start` line — it should use slotEndTime. As a result, `end > workingHour.endTime` can never be true when start is inside the working hours, so a slot that starts within working hours but ends after the end of the host's working day is treated as inside working hours and remains bookable, cutting into time the host has marked unavailable.

findings.title: Working-hours minutes compared against slot's UTC wall clock
findings.body: In the new working-hours check, `slotStartTime` is `time.utc()` and `start`/`end` are computed from `slotStartTime.hour()` — i.e. minutes since midnight UTC. `workingHour.startTime`/`endTime`, however, are minutes since midnight in the organizer's (schedule) timezone, as produced by getUserAvailability/getWorkingHours. Comparing the two directly only works when the organizer is in UTC; for any other timezone the check accepts or rejects slots at shifted times. For example an organizer with 9:00–17:00 IST availability (240–690 minutes UTC) compared against a slot's UTC wall clock will pass/fail on the wrong boundary, so fixed-host slots can be shown outside their actual working hours or wrongly hidden.
